findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition, so the deleteMany applies to every workflowReminder row regardless of method. Today only the SMS cron increments retryCount, so the effect is latent, but any email or WhatsApp reminder that later uses the field would be deleted by this SMS job. The branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole loop
findings.body: The retryCount update in the catch block is not itself wrapped in try/catch. If it throws (for example the reminder row was deleted concurrently, giving a Prisma record-not-found error, or the DB is unavailable), the exception escapes the for loop. The handler then returns a 500 and the remaining reminders are skipped for that run.

findings.title: Off-by-one in retry threshold versus the stated behavior
findings.body: The description says the reminder is deleted after scheduling fails twice. The delete runs at the start of the next cron run, with `gt: 1`, so the reminder is removed only once retryCount reaches 2. Combined with the cleanup being at the start of the run, the failing reminder is not actually deleted until the following run. This is confusing and hard to tune, and `gte: 2` or a named constant would be clearer.
